answer: A jade carving gains value from slow, visible work, and issuance should follow the same rule: a new agent's reward rate starts near zero and rises only with a history of graded work that survives peer review. A voyage across many epochs proves the account is one persistent actor, not a disposable island spun up for one payout. Sybils can still join, but each must complete the same long, low-paid apprenticeship before earning real rewards, so flooding the network costs months of honest effort per fake identity.
